Narrative
fields.value:
The risk is a three-story, joisted masonry (ISO 2) mixed-use building containing eight apartments and two commercial occupancies consisting of a restaurant and spa/beauty salon. One apartment is currently vacant and offered for rent as normal tenant turnover. The building contains approximately 10,784 square feet, including a small finished basement area.

The building underwent a gut rehabilitation in 2005, including electrical, plumbing, and heating upgrades. Electrical service consists of BX cable and conduit with circuit-breaker protection. No Zinsco or Stab-Lok panels were observed. An open electrical panel box and stored materials obstructing access to basement electrical panels were noted and should be corrected. Heating is provided by low-pressure steam boilers, with wall-sleeve air conditioning for residential areas and forced-air units for the commercial spaces. A leaking basement hot-water heater was noted and was scheduled for replacement.

The exterior is brick, and the wood-joist roof with rolled-asphalt covering appears to be in good condition. Roof renovations were completed in 2021 and 2026, and no active leaks were observed. Tenant items are stored directly on the roof surface at a third-floor balcony area without protective material, creating potential for damage to the roof covering. No structural or exterior issues were otherwise noted, and there are no current or planned renovations.

The restaurant contains a full commercial cooking line with deep fryers equipped with stainless-steel baffles. The cooking line is protected by an exhaust hood with baffle-type filters and a UL 300-compliant wet-chemical automatic extinguishing system. The hood is properly cleaned and maintained, the extinguishing system is currently tagged, and a K-class fire extinguisher is present. Commercial cooking exposures appear to be appropriately controlled.

The building is fully sprinklered with a wet-pipe system. There is no central station fire alarm. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are present in the residential and commercial areas. Fire extinguishers are provided throughout; however, some were noted to be unmounted or lacking current service tags and should be corrected. No central station burglar alarm was observed. No previous losses, fires, security incidents, or structural issues were noted. Overall housekeeping and maintenance are average.

fields.label: 4. Type of stucco, if any (if building is stucco-clad, include CLOSE-UP INTERIOR PHOTOS showing the depth of window and/or door openings)?
5. If EIFS-clad, is it a Face-sealed (barrier) EIFS Assembly or a Drainable EIFS Assembly?
fields.help: Instructions A Face-sealed EIFS Assembly is a total barrier system, using caulk or other sealant to prevent water from getting behind the stucco. The problem with this system is that, given the typically high number of joints and other openings, including vents, the likelihood of seal failure is high (either from defective application or eventual sealant breakdown) and, with that, water frequently becomes trapped, leading to moisture-related mold &/or dry rot. A Drainable EIFS Assembly, on the other hand, includes water channels, whereby any water that may get behind the stucco, can escape, thus avoiding any moisture-related mold &/or dry rot problems. As part of your EIFS inspection, look for water channels &/or metal weep screeds (with weep holes for water escape, on the underside) at the exposed bottom of the stucco application. Especially important is that the stucco does not extend all the way to the ground, where it (as well as the weep screed) can be covered by mulch or dirt.

fields.label: 28. Is risk free of Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok type electrical panels & circuit breakers- MOVE CURSOR OVER TEXT FOR DETAILS (if No, provide a CLOSE-UP PHOTO SHOWING "STAB-LOK" ON THE LABEL?
fields.help: Instructions Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok type electric panels have a history of breakers not tripping when they should. Due to design or other problems, two-pole FPE Stab-Lok circuit breakers (the type that would feed clothes dryers, for example) do not always work reliably, and, in some studies, they have been noted to fail 30% or more of the time. Identifying an FPE Stab-Lok panel is easy. Simply look for Federal Pacific & the Stab-Lok logo either on the inside or outside of the panel door.

fields.label: 29. Is risk free of GTE Sylvania Zinsco circuit breakers- MOVE CURSOR OVER TEXT FOR DETAILS (if No, provide a CLOSE-UP PHOTO SHOWING "Sylvania Zinsco" label)?
fields.help: Instructions GTE-Sylvania Zinsco breakers have a history of breakers not tripping when they should. The problem is that the circuit breakers inside many Zinsco panels melt to the main bus bar, rendering the breaker unable to trip, even when theres a short or overloaded circuit, with the net result, given a surge of power, wires melt and a fire ensues. Identifying a GTE-Sylvania Zinsco breaker is easy. Simply look for the "GTE-Sylvania" &/or "Zinsco" label anywhere on the panel. Additionally, Zinsco breakers have color-coded toggle switches (15 amps blue; 20 amp red or orange; 30 amp green; 40 amp grey).

fields.label: 30. Is risk free of extension cord overuse?
fields.help: Instructions Extension cords should never be permanently coonected to large appliances e.g. a refrigerator or an air conditioning unit.
